paragraphs.text: DeepSeek Harness plugin: recall a message, go back to an earlier reply, or edit an AI reply in a cop
y of the conversation.
# dsh-history-edit

Conversation history edits for DeepSeek Harness (DSH):
change what you said, go back to an earlier p
oint, or fix an AI reply, without losing anything.
> **Maintenance: best-effort.** Issues may go unanswered; forks are welcome.
## What it adds to the chat

- **Recall** (under each of your messages). Goes back to just before that message and puts its
text

back in the message box, to resend as is, changed, or with files. Nothing is deleted: when
you send

the next message, the recalled message and everything after it are set aside.
- **Edit again** (on a

message that was edited through the `rewrite` method of the channel below).
Opens an edit window; t

he edited message replaces the old one and the AI answers again. If later
messages of yours exist, a

**copy** of the conversation is created instead, so nothing is lost,
and the page opens it.
- **Go

back here** (under an AI reply that has later turns). The next message you send restarts
from that r

eply and the later turns are set aside. A banner says so and has a **Cancel** button.
- **Edit reply

** (under an AI reply). Creates a copy of the conversation up to that turn with the
reply text chang
ed; the original stays as it was, and the page opens the copy.
"Set aside" means hidden from the AI and from the chat page. The events stay in the session log.

The interface is in English, and in French when the page language is French. To add a language,
add
a table to `STRINGS` at the top of `client.js` (missing keys fall back to English).
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Restart the profile afterwards. Requires Node `^22.19.0 || >=24` and DSH `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0`
(see

Compatibility). Once the package is on npm, `dsh plugin --profile web add
dsh-history-edit` works to

mpatibility). Once the package is on npm, `dsh plugin --profile web add
dsh-history-edit` works too.
The plugin has no configuration.
## How it works

- The DSH session log is append-only. A message can carry `surfaceOp: replace {startSeq, endSeq}`:
i

t takes the place of that range of events in what the model sees (the "surface"). Editing and
going

back both write one such message; nothing is ever removed from the log.
- `lib/history.js` holds the

reasoning over the log as pure functions (which turn a message is in,
which range an edit or a go-b

ack replaces, whether a reply can be edited, how an edited reply
event looks). It has no dependency

and is covered by `tests/`.
- `index.js` (host side) reads the session through DSH, calls `lib/histo

ry.js`, and writes the
result. It serves a small JSON channel at `/dsh-history/<method>` (`list`, `r

ewrite`, `rewind`,
`cancelRewind`, `editReply`, `canEdit`), protected by DSH's own connection check

(Host/Origin
fence and browser token).
- `client.js` (page side) draws the buttons, the edit window

and the banner, and hides the turns
that were set aside. It finds the chat rows through the `data-ch

at-flow-kind`,
`data-chat-anchor-key` and `data-chat-turn` attributes of DSH's chat page.
## Compatibility
| Component | Supported |
ptional `peerDependencies` on `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm` and `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`, the only DSH pa

ckages the host side imports |
| Platform | Linux (tested); pure JavaScript, no native addon |
| Pag
e | the chat page of DSH's web UI; the buttons depend on its row attributes and may need an update w
hen the page changes |
Tested with DSH `0.2.0-rc.2` on Node 22.23 (see Verification).
## Permissions and external services
Everything the plugin can touch, and what happens when it fails:
| Capability | Where | Used for | If it fails |
| **Files** | `index.js` (`realpathSync`) | resolves the path of the running `dsh` binary, to find D

SH's own packages; the plugin reads and writes no other file itself | the plugin fails to load |
| *
*Session log** | `index.js` (through `ctx.agents`, `ctx.sessionController`) | reads the events of a
conversation; appends the edited message, and creates a copy of the conversation (new session) for a
n edit in a copy or an edited reply. This is the plugin's purpose | the operation returns an error c

ode and the page shows a message; the original conversation is not touched |
| **Network** | none |

nothing leaves the computer | n/a |
| **Commands** | none | no child process, no shell | n/a |
| **H
TTP route** | `index.js` (`ctx.webServer.register`) | `POST /dsh-history/<method>` for the page, beh
ind `ctx.connection.admit()` (DSH's Host/Origin fence and token); bodies are limited to 1 MiB and mu

st be JSON | non-admitted requests get 401/403; other errors are returned as JSON |
| **Dynamic modu
le loading** | `index.js` (`importFromDsh`) | loads `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm` (to build a user message)
and `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` (the empty config schema) from the DSH installation that runs the pl
ugin (a synchronous `require` of an ES module fails on Node 22). Nothing is downloaded and no code i

s evaluated from text (`eval` / `new Function` are not used) | the plugin fails to load |
| **Hook o
n the agent loop** | `index.js` (`agent/pre-step`) | when you confirm an edit or a go-back, the next
user message is written as a replacement. For that, the plugin wraps `session.append` of that one c
onversation until the message is written, then removes the wrapper (also on abort or if the session
is closed) | the edit is not applied and the error is reported; a go-back that cannot be computed is
dropped and the message is sent normally |
The plugin adds no tool for the model and no setting.
## Verification

Checked on a disposable profile (`DSH_HOME` pointing at a temporary folder, profile cloned with
`dsh
<name> --from-default-profile web`, so the real profile is never touched):
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`npm test` runs 24 standalone tests of `lib/history.js` (turn outline, edit plans, go-back ranges,
r

eply cuts, edited replies, contiguity errors) with no DSH installation needed. The module is a
JavaS

cript port of the logic that first ran in a native addon; the port was compared with that
addon on a
bout 2.2 million generated and real-log cases with identical results.
